land.text: the northern edge of the Chacoan land in the San Juan Basin, where Salmon and Aztec Ruins were built 'during a thirty-year wet period commencing in 1100'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria starts the Aztec row the year after the Chaco row ends; the pages do not date a hand-over.

capitals.name: Aztec Ruins (Aztec, New Mexico)
capitals.note: The page gives the monument's coordinates (36.8358 N, 107.9981 W, San Juan County) but never calls the site a capital; the dot marks the system's namesake centre.

keyframe_review.note: unverified: page budget. 1152-1293, 8,739 km2. No page gives an extent or an area for the Aztec system (the monument itself is 318 acres); the pages date the ruins to 'the 12th and 13th centuries' and to a wet period 'commencing in 1100'. The shape's cell footprint (about -109.8 to -108.06 longitude, 36.73 to 37.58 latitude) lies north and west of the ruins, which the page puts at 36.836 N, 107.998 W, so the namesake site sits on its eastern edge; kept, with the extent west and north of the ruins resting on Cliopatria alone.

unverified: page budget. 1294-1304, the same 8,739 km2 as the 1152 shape. Nothing on any page opened explains a change in 1294 (Cliopatria splits the row though the Seshat seed carries one id, us_aztec_puebloan); 'The Ancestral Puebloans left their established homes in the 12th and 13th centuries', so the system is already emptying or empty by about 1300.

region.text: the northern San Juan country around Aztec Ruins on the Animas River

ledger.note: 1152: the Aztec regional system stands on the old Chaco north. The Chaco page: Salmon and Aztec Ruins 'were built during a thirty-year wet period commencing in 1100'; the Aztec Ruins page: 'Archaeological evidence puts the construction of the ruins in the 12th and 13th centuries'. Neither page gives 1152, which is Cliopatria's start (the year after the Chaco row ends); Chaco's 'cohesive' system 'began to unravel around 1140'.

1304: the Ancestral Puebloan system of the northern San Juan is gone. The page: 'The Ancestral Puebloans left their established homes in the 12th and 13th centuries' and 'merged into the various Pueblo peoples whose descendants still live in Arizona and New Mexico'. No page opened dates the Aztec abandonment; 1304 is Cliopatria's last year (the page's centuries end 1300).

certainty.note: No page gives frontiers; the extent is Cliopatria's approximate footprint of a regional system of great houses.

sources.title: Ancestral Puebloans
sources.note: The abandonment of homes in the 12th and 13th centuries and the merging into the Pueblo peoples; says nothing of Aztec Ruins beyond a list of monuments.

sources.title: Chaco Culture National Historical Park
sources.note: Salmon and Aztec Ruins built in the thirty-year wet period from 1100; the unravelling of the Chacoan system from about 1140.

sources.title: Aztec Ruins National Monument
sources.note: Construction in the 12th and 13th centuries; coordinates and county; thin (no occupation or abandonment dates, no extent).

notes: Type 'culture' for the same reason as the Chaco dossier: the pages name no state. Wikidata Q478805 is shared with puebloans-chaco-regional-system; kept as a separate dossier (Cliopatria and Seshat code a separate Aztec system, ids us_aztec_puebloan versus us_chaco_1/2, with a different and much smaller shape starting the year after Chaco's), but the pages treat both as the Ancestral Puebloans and say the Aztec Ruins were built as a Chaco north outlier from 1100, so a reviewer may merge them under the Chaco slug with both Names. Page budget 1-2: only the Aztec Ruins National Monument page was opened for this state beyond the two shared pages, and it is thin (no abandonment, no extent, no mention of Chaco or Mesa Verde); both shapes are therefore unverified and both events are confidence 1 ('page silent'). A gap-filler should open the Mesa Verde National Park, Salmon Ruins and Seshat pages for the 1150-1300 dates (the gazetteer's places Mesa Verde and Farmington both fall inside the shape, which the Aztec Ruins page does not cover). The Aztec Ruins site is not in the gazetteer's places; the capital uses the page's coordinates. Gazetteer names needed: place 'Aztec Ruins' (36.836 N, 107.998 W).
